headline: v5 changes the artifact's thesis. Where v2 through v4 said no live gate owns these classes, v5 says the product law stays on v3 while test execution rides DR-G20 and DR-G21, and claims D-056 gates 2 and 3 are thereby answered. The split is a real, adopted pattern and this is the most promising route the family has found. But the mechanism that makes that pattern lawful — the classes being named at the obligation — does not exist for DR-133, and two of the seven classes do not ride the fragments cited for them.

precedentAudit.conclusion: The precedent is real, adopted, and reviewed, and v5 characterises it accurately. Law on the contract plus execution at an existing gate is a lawful shape for a D-056 remainder. That is a genuine advance over v3 and v4, which routed everything to a new DR-G* row and therefore to a D-002 required-gate-set change. I want that on the record: the thesis is better, and the first blocker is about the step it skipped, not about the shape.

blockers.title: The artifact claims D-056 gates 2 and 3 are answered, but nothing at DR-G20 or DR-G21 names DR-133 or its NT classes, and the precedent it relies on is precedent for the naming act it has not performed
blockers.finding: doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone now reads 'This candidate proposes that leftover-design is closed as execution remainder under D-056 gates 2 and 3.' Gate 3, in the pinned D-056 turn-2 subject, is: 'Each such remainder is already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner.' The operative words are already named. Measured against live bytes: gate-harness-naming.v3 does not contain the string DR-133 anywhere in the file; neither its DR-G20 entry nor its DR-G21 entry mentions DR-133 or any NT id; and neither file 08's DR-G20 row nor its DR-G21 row mentions DR-133. So the remainder is named in this candidate and nowhere else. The contrast with the artifact's own canonical example is exact and decisive. DR-102's split works because D-086's DR-G21 entry says 'DR-102 CC-1..CC-11 execute here (control-protocol-contract.v2 ID-DEP-3)' — the classes are named at the obligation, in an adopted artifact, before D-085 relied on the split. v5 asserts the equivalent mapping for DR-133 without that step having happened, so it is proposing the naming and simultaneously treating it as already done. There is a second limb, and it is self-inflicted by the same gap. Gate 2 excludes from the splittable remainder the 'authoring of fixtures, schemas, successors, actor-joins, missing design'. Since this join requires a later D-086 successor to name NT-1..NT-7 at their gates, today's remainder includes authoring that successor, which gate 2 forbids. Gate 2 becomes satisfiable only after that successor lands, at which point the remainder really is execution alone.
blockers.whyBlocker: This is the claim that would move DR-133 from leftover-design to two gates from eligibility. Recording it as written would put on the register's record that gate 3 is answered by a naming that does not exist, which is precisely the false-ownership failure this family has been iterating away from since v1. It is also stronger than the v1 error, because it comes attached to a correct precedent that would make a reviewer likelier to accept it.
blockers.repair: Keep the thesis and add the missing step. Say that the execution remainder for the classes that genuinely ride is capable of riding DR-G20 and DR-G21, that D-056 gates 2 and 3 become satisfiable only once a later D-086 successor amends those gate entries to name DR-133 NT-1..NT-7 the way DR-102's CC-1..CC-11 are named at DR-G21, and record that successor as the owed act with its owner. Then change doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone back to a statement that the leftover is not closed today. This route is materially lighter than the new-DR-G*-row path v3 and v4 proposed — no new gate, no D-002 required-gate-set change — and on the classes that ride it is likely the right answer; it simply has one act in front of it.

blockers.title: NT-3 and NT-5 do not ride the fragments cited for them: both fragments are DR-G21 retained evidence about post-fault behaviour, and neither class is an input in G21's fault corpus
blockers.finding: The named attack for this turn is whether the execution remainder actually rides the quoted fragment. I checked each class against the field its fragment comes from. NT-1 cites 'malformed/truncated/duplicate/EOF' and NT-2 cites 'malformed/truncated'; both are in G21's harnessVerbatim, which is the corpus — an out-of-vocabulary frame and an extra member on a closed payload are malformed inputs, so those two ride, and I accept them. NT-4 cites G20's 'no direct UI/unstructured logs/final authority' and D-086's 'authority escape', and NT-7 cites the latter; those are properties G20 must establish, and establishing that a component cannot take final authority requires exercising attempts at it, so I accept those two as well. NT-3 and NT-5 are different in kind. NT-3 cites 'candidate discard' and NT-5 cites 'Coverage/D9/UI/exit goldens'; both come from G21's requiredRetainedEvidenceVerbatim, not from its corpus. G21's corpus is a list of fault classes — crash, panic, timeout, resource, malformed, truncated, duplicate, EOF, process-tree, recovery — and neither of these classes is one. v3's NT-3 input is a FactCandidateV1 whose relationSchemaId or payload is provider-minted or mismatched, and its pass is 'Host-owned relation registry rejects before fact admission'; that is a well-formed frame refused on semantics, not a malformed one. G21's 'candidate discard' is discarding uncommitted candidates so that a failure cannot leak them — a different trigger and a different mechanism. v3's NT-5 input is a Coverage payload that narrows, widens, or converts unknown to covered, and its pass is host refusal of the domain mutation; G21's Coverage goldens show that Coverage output stays honest across its fault corpus. Running G21's corpus to completion would never exercise either pass condition. The artifact's own predecessor said exactly this about exactly these fragments: v4's NT-3 read 'G21 discards uncommitted candidates so a crash cannot leak them. It does not own relation-registry admission of FactCandidate content', and its NT-5 read 'G21 Coverage goldens are containment/honesty after fault. They do not own host refusal of Coverage-domain mutation at admission.' v5 reverses both without acknowledging the reversal or explaining what changed. A lesser instance: NT-6 also cites the retained-evidence goldens fragment, although its own input — 'a constructible extra member or out-of-vocabulary frame carrying a D9 class' — is malformed-shaped and would ride the corpus fragment its siblings cite. That one is mis-cited rather than unsupported.
blockers.whyBlocker: The whole value of the execution-remainder thesis is that the pass conditions are actually exercised somewhere. For two of seven classes they are not, so naming them at G21 in a later successor would name them at a gate whose corpus cannot reach them, and a SATISFIED cycle relying on this join would record execution coverage that does not exist. Five of seven riding is real progress; two not riding is not a wording problem.
blockers.repair: Split the answer. Keep NT-1, NT-2, NT-4, NT-7 as execution rides on G21 and G20 respectively, and re-cite NT-6 to the corpus fragment that carries it. For NT-3 and NT-5, either identify a corpus fragment that genuinely exercises semantic refusal of well-formed input at admission — I did not find one in any of the 22 live gates — or state that these two remain leftover-design pending an obligation whose corpus includes hostile-but-well-formed admission inputs. If v5 believes v4's contrary characterisation of these fragments was wrong, say so in terms and give the reason; a silent reversal between successive versions of the same artifact is the thing a reviewer cannot let pass.

acceptRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. With 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX the verdict is REJECT.

independence.otherReviewerHandling: Codex verdicts for v1 through v4 exist on disk; none was opened. CODEX-PONGJ-V4-SF1 is known to me only as an id and the prompt's phrasing, so I judged v5's execution-remainder work on its own terms.
independence.priorPositions: I rejected v1 and v2, accepted v3, and rejected v4. v5 reverses the thesis I accepted at v3 and reasserts a version of the gate joins I rejected at v1, so the risk this turn runs both ways: rejecting reflexively because it resembles v1, or accepting because the new precedent is genuine and the family is five versions deep. I guarded both. I verified the DR-102 precedent at three independent sources and say plainly that the thesis is better than v3's and v4's. I then resolved every per-class fragment to the specific field it came from, which is what separates the four classes that ride from the two that do not, and I accepted four of seven rides rather than rejecting the mechanism wholesale.
independence.notEscalated: I did not charge NT-4 and NT-7 despite their fragments being properties rather than corpus classes, because establishing 'no final authority' and 'no authority escape' requires exercising attempts; and I did not charge NT-6 separately, because a correct citation exists in the same row.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Fourteen attacks run, five landed. Custody is clean and the quotation discipline is now excellent: 24 of 24 gate cells, the DR-133 evidence cell and both D-086 executes strings are byte-exact, every per-class fragment really occurs in the source it is attributed to, and the 22-gate arithmetic checks out at 20 plus 2 against exactly 22 live rows. v5 also changes the artifact's thesis, and the change is an improvement I want on the record. Instead of routing everything to a new DR-G* row — which is a D-002 required-gate-set change and the heaviest act in the family so far — it splits product law from test execution: the law stays on provider-only-output-contract.v3 and the execution rides existing gates. That pattern is real. I verified at three independent sources that DR-102's law sits on control-protocol-contract.v2, that D-085 recorded DR-102 SATISFIED with CC-1..CC-11 execution remaining at DR-G21, and that D-086's DR-G21 entry says in terms 'DR-102 CC-1..CC-11 execute here'. What blocks is that the step which makes that precedent lawful has not been taken. D-056 gate 3 requires the remainder to be already named as a condition-4 obligation with an owner. Measured: the string DR-133 does not appear anywhere in gate-harness-naming.v3, neither its DR-G20 nor its DR-G21 entry names DR-133 or any NT, and neither file-08 row does either. The mapping exists in this candidate and nowhere else, so the artifact is proposing the naming and treating it as already done. The same gap defeats its gate-2 claim, since gate 2 excludes authoring a successor from the splittable remainder and this join needs a D-086 successor to exist. The second blocker is narrower and concerns whether the classes actually ride. I resolved each fragment to its field. NT-1 and NT-2 cite G21's corpus and genuinely ride it; NT-4 and NT-7 cite G20's final-authority and authority-escape properties, which cannot be established without exercising attempts, and I accept those too. NT-3 and NT-5 cite G21 retained evidence — candidate discard and Coverage goldens — while their own inputs are well-formed frames refused on semantics, which appear nowhere in G21's fault corpus of crash, panic, timeout, resource, malformed, truncated, duplicate, EOF, process-tree and recovery. Running that corpus to completion would never exercise either pass condition. v4 said exactly this about exactly these fragments and v5 reverses it without a word. NT-6 cites the same evidence fragment although its own malformed-shaped input would ride the corpus fragment its siblings use; that one is mis-cited rather than unsupported. The SHOULD-FIX is three findingDisposition entries pointing at fields that are gone or hollow, including one I asked to have corrected at v4. A v6 that keeps the thesis, keeps the four rides that hold, re-cites NT-6, says plainly that gates 2 and 3 become satisfiable only after a D-086 successor names DR-133 NT-1..NT-7 at their gates the way DR-102's classes are named, and either finds a corpus that reaches NT-3 and NT-5 or leaves those two as leftover-design, would be a strong artifact — and a materially shorter path to eligibility than anything v3 or v4 proposed.
